name: New York City: DOB, DCWP and EPA rules read from official pages
note: Every rule was read on its source_url on the checked_on date. The DOB pages show no last-updated date, so checked_on is the date they were read, not the date DOB last changed them. A rule that does not match the facts given, or whose conditions are not all known, is reported as unknown_confirm. Exemption from a permit never removes other obligations: licensing, zoning, landmarks, other agencies, and related filings.

trade_notes.partition: New partition walls are not on DOB's permit-exempt list (DOB 'Do I need a permit' page and 1 RCNY 101-14 read 2026-10-19). That does not say a permit is required; confirm with a registered design professional or DOB.
trade_notes.stairs: No verified rule is held for stairs. Stairs are structural and code-governed; confirm with a registered design professional.
trade_notes.carpentry: Trim, baseboard and door installation have no rule in this file.
trade_notes.tiling: Wall and floor tile have no rule in this file.

rules.summary: Electrical work must be done by a NYC Licensed Master Electrician (LME). No owner exemption is described.
rules.citation: NYC DOB, Electrical work: project requirements for owners
rules.notes: Minor electrical work also needs an LME and a permit.

rules.summary: No installation or modification of electrical systems without a permit. General electrical work also gets a DOB inspection; minor work needs the permit but no DOB inspection.
rules.citation: NYC DOB, Electrical work: project requirements for owners
rules.notes: Installations of 1,000 kVA or more need a registered design professional to file construction documents. This tool does not size electrical loads.

rules.summary: Plumbing and fuel gas piping work listed on the DOB page can only be performed by a NYC Licensed Master Plumber (LMP). The page does not address owners doing their own plumbing.
rules.citation: NYC DOB, Plumbing work: project requirements for owners
rules.notes: Plumbing fixture replacement needs an LMP even though it needs no permit (see NYC-PLUMB-PERMIT-001).

rules.summary: Plumbing fixture replacement is on DOB's list of work that does not need a permit. The page does not say 'bathroom' and sets no size limit.

conditions.text: The plumbing work is only replacing existing fixtures, with no new or moved supply, drain, vent or gas piping.

rules.citation: NYC DOB, Do I need a permit? (work that does not require a permit)
rules.notes: Other plumbing work: no verified permit rule is held here, so it stays unknown_confirm.

rules.summary: Painting is on DOB's list of work that does not need a permit. No limits are listed.
rules.citation: NYC DOB, Do I need a permit? (work that does not require a permit)
rules.notes: Lead-safe rules can still apply (see the EPA rules).

rules.summary: Plastering is on DOB's list of work that does not need a permit. No limits are listed.
rules.citation: NYC DOB, Do I need a permit? (work that does not require a permit)
rules.notes: Lead-safe rules can still apply (see the EPA rules).

rules.summary: Installing new cabinets is on DOB's list of work that does not need a permit. DOB's footnote says contractors must be licensed through DCWP.
rules.citation: NYC DOB, Do I need a permit? (work that does not require a permit)

rules.summary: Resurfacing floors is on DOB's list of work that does not need a permit. DOB's footnote says contractors must be licensed through DCWP.

conditions.text: The floor work is resurfacing or refinishing an existing floor, with no subfloor, joist or structural repair.

rules.citation: NYC DOB, Do I need a permit? (work that does not require a permit)
rules.notes: New flooring over a changed subfloor is not covered by this rule.

rules.summary: Non-structural roof repair is on DOB's list of work that does not need a permit.

conditions.text: The roof work is non-structural repair only.

rules.citation: NYC DOB, Do I need a permit? (work that does not require a permit)

rules.summary: Permanent removal of a non-load-bearing, non-fire-rated partition in a Group R occupancy needs no permit when the removed part is the lesser of 50 percent of that wall surface or 45 square feet.

conditions.text: The building is a Group R occupancy (residential).
The wall is an interior partition, not an exterior wall.
The wall is not load-bearing (needs an engineer).
The removed part is at most 50 percent of that wall surface.
The removed part is at most 45 square feet.

The dwelling unit is not in the Special Hudson Yards District, Preservation Area P-2 of the Special Garment Center District, the Special Clinton District, the Special West Chelsea District or the Greenpoint-Williamsburg anti-harassment areas, and is not in a single room occupancy multiple dwelling.

rules.notes: The rule's exception text joins its two conditions with 'either' and 'and'; this file treats the exception as applying if the area or the single room occupancy condition holds, the cautious reading. Changing the layout of rooms in an exception area is a material alteration that needs a permit. The exemption does not remove the duty to file for related structural, electrical or plumbing work.

rules.summary: A contractor doing home improvement work (remodeling or repairs) needs a DCWP Home Improvement Contractor (HIC) license, and gives the license number when obtaining a DOB permit.

conditions.text: A contractor, not the owner, does the work.

rules.citation: NYC DOB, Home Improvement Contractor permit requirements; NYC DCWP home improvement licensing page
rules.notes: DCWP says the license is needed for work that costs more than $200 and does not cover new home construction, plumbing or purely electrical work. DOB's footnote names cabinets and floor resurfacing explicitly; the other trades fall under DCWP's wording 'remodeling or repairs', which does not list trades, so confirm the trade with DCWP (https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/consumers/shopping-services-home-improvement.page, read 2026-10-19).

rules.summary: A homeowner doing their own work does not need an HIC license.

conditions.text: The homeowner does the work personally.

rules.citation: NYC DOB, Home Improvement Contractor permit requirements
rules.notes: This is about the HIC license only. It does not exempt electrical or plumbing work from the LME and LMP rules.

rules.summary: No work requiring a permit can be performed by a General Contractor without the owner first hiring a Registered Design Professional (RDP) to file the drawings.

conditions.text: The work needs a DOB permit.

rules.citation: NYC DOB, Alteration project requirements for owners (residential)
rules.notes: Work that stays inside the exempt categories needs no permit and so no RDP filing.

rules.summary: Paid work that disturbs more than 6 square feet of paint per room inside (20 square feet outside) in housing built before 1978 must be done by an EPA RRP-certified firm using lead-safe work practices.

conditions.text: Someone is paid to do the work.
The work disturbs more than 6 square feet of paint in a room (interior).

rules.citation: EPA Renovation, Repair and Painting (RRP) Rule, contractors page and 2026 small entity compliance guide
rules.notes: The EPA contractor page does not address owner-occupants doing their own unpaid work. Exterior limit is 20 square feet.

rules.summary: Window replacement and demolition in paid work on pre-1978 housing are covered by the RRP Rule whatever the area of paint disturbed.

conditions.text: Someone is paid to do the work.
The work is window replacement or demolition.

rules.citation: EPA Renovation, Repair and Painting (RRP) Rule, 2026 small entity compliance guide
rules.notes: Read from the EPA guide as summarized on 2026-10-19; re-read the guide text before relying on this rule.
